questions.stem: Who was the FIRST INDIAN WOMAN to receive the Bharat Ratna?

options.option_text: Lata Mangeshkar — legendary playback singer (2001)
Indira Gandhi — Prime Minister of India (1971)
M.S. Subbulakshmi — Carnatic music maestro (1998)
Aruna Asaf Ali — freedom movement leader (1997)

questions.explanation: Indira Gandhi received the Bharat Ratna in 1971, making her the first Indian woman awardee. M.S. Subbulakshmi (1998) is a common wrong pick as she is celebrated as the first woman to perform at the UN General Assembly — not the first Bharat Ratna woman. Mother Teresa (1980) also predates Subbulakshmi but was a non-Indian citizen, so Indira Gandhi remains the first Indian woman recipient.

questions.stem: On which occasion are the PADMA AWARDS announced by the Government of India every year?

options.option_text: Republic Day eve (25th January every year)
Independence Day eve (14th August every year)
National Science Day (28th February every year)
Constitution Day evening (26th November every year)

questions.explanation: Padma Awards are announced on the eve of Republic Day (25th January) each year and are presented by the President at Rashtrapati Bhavan. Independence Day (15th August) is a common confusion — that occasion is used for different recognitions such as gallantry medal announcements. Constitution Day (26th November) marks adoption of the Constitution and carries no Padma association.

questions.stem: The Bharat Ratna was awarded POSTHUMOUSLY for the very FIRST TIME to which recipient?

options.option_text: Mahatma Gandhi — Father of the Nation (1869–1948)
Vinoba Bhave — Bhoodan movement leader (awarded 1983)
Lal Bahadur Shastri — second Prime Minister (awarded 1966)
Rajiv Gandhi — sixth Prime Minister (awarded 1991)

questions.explanation: Lal Bahadur Shastri, who died in Tashkent (January 1966), was the first to receive the Bharat Ratna posthumously — the same year. Vinoba Bhave (1983) and Rajiv Gandhi (1991) also received it posthumously, but came later. Mahatma Gandhi, notably, has never been officially awarded the Bharat Ratna despite multiple recommendations — a fact examiners use as a trap.

questions.stem: The PADMA AWARDS were suspended between 1977 and 1980. Which government took this decision?

options.option_text: The Rajiv Gandhi government amid post-Emergency reforms
The VP Singh National Front government in 1989–1990
The IK Gujral United Front minority coalition (1997)
The Janata Party government of PM Morarji Desai (1977)

questions.explanation: The Janata Party government (1977–79) under PM Morarji Desai suspended both the Bharat Ratna and Padma Awards, viewing them as incompatible with egalitarian democratic principles. Awards were revived in 1980 when Indira Gandhi returned to power. The VP Singh government also briefly discontinued them (1990–91), which causes confusion — but the prominent first suspension belongs to the Janata Party.

questions.stem: In which year was the scope of the BHARAT RATNA formally AMENDED to cover 'any field of human endeavour', paving the way for awards to sportspersons?

options.option_text: 2001 — coinciding with Lata Mangeshkar's Bharat Ratna honour
2011 — broadening eligibility beyond arts and science
2008 — following Abhinav Bindra's Olympic gold medal
2013 — timed with Sachin Tendulkar's retirement announcement

questions.explanation: The Bharat Ratna statutes were amended in December 2011 to include 'any field of human endeavour', enabling Sachin Tendulkar's award in 2014. Before 2011, the award was officially restricted to arts, literature, science, and public services. Many candidates confuse 2013 or 2014 (Tendulkar's actual award year) as the amendment year — the rule change and the first sportsperson award are two separate events.

questions.stem: Which scientist received the Bharat Ratna in the INAUGURAL 1954 batch AND had previously won the Nobel Prize for Physics?

options.option_text: Homi J. Bhabha — architect of India's nuclear research programme
Satyendra Nath Bose — pioneer of Bose-Einstein statistics
CV Raman — first Asian Nobel Laureate in Physics (1930)
Meghnad Saha — thermal ionization equation in astrophysics

questions.explanation: CV Raman won the Nobel Prize in Physics (1930) for the Raman Effect and was one of just three inaugural Bharat Ratna recipients in 1954 (alongside C. Rajagopalachari and S. Radhakrishnan). Homi Bhabha received the Padma Bhushan in 1954 but never the Bharat Ratna — a very common confusion. Satyendra Nath Bose received the Padma Vibhushan (1954) but not Bharat Ratna, which remains a matter of historical debate.

questions.stem: Under Article 18 of the Indian Constitution, which specific RESTRICTION governs the use of civilian honours such as the Bharat Ratna?

options.option_text: The award title cannot be used as a name prefix or suffix
The award cannot be conferred on active serving government servants
Recipients must formally donate the cash component to a state fund
The President alone decides awardees without any Ministerial advice

questions.explanation: Article 18 abolishes titles but does NOT prohibit civilian awards — however, the Bharat Ratna statutes explicitly bar recipients from using 'Bharat Ratna' or any Padma award name as a prefix or suffix to their name. The Supreme Court upheld the validity of Padma Awards in 1996, drawing this precise distinction. Option B is wrong — civil servants routinely receive Padma awards. Option D is wrong — the PM recommends names to the President.
